card.title: Manufacture of sodium hydroxide by Diaphragm Cell

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The diaphragm cell electrolyses concentrated brine into three sellable products — Cl₂ at the anode, H₂ at the cathode, NaOH in the catholyte — whose mutual incompatibility makes the asbestos diaphragm the product specification itself.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Anode: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻; Cathode: 2H₂O + 2e⁻ → H₂ + 2OH⁻ - Parasitic: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Covers only: manufacture of sodium hydroxide by diaphragm cell (within Modern Chemical Manufactures).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The diaphragm is not a detail - it is the product specification.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Two cells, one difference*** - aqueous brine gives NaOH (water wins the cathode); molten NaCl gives Na metal (no water to win) - the Downs and diaphragm cells differ by one phase.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Sodium Hydroxide by the Diaphragm Cell Caustic soda is manufactured by **electrolysing concentrated brine** in the diaphragm cell: chlorine at the anode, hydrogen at the cathode, and sodium hydroxide accumulating in the cathode compartment — with an **asbestos diaphragm** keeping the three products apart. The cell is simultaneously an electrochemistry lesson and a separation problem.  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Overall:** 2NaCl + 2H₂O --electrolysis--> 2NaOH + Cl₂(g) + H₂(g). - **Anode (graphite or coated titanium):** 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻ — chlorine gas evolved. - **Cathode (steel mesh):** 2H₂O + 2e⁻ → H₂ + 2OH⁻ — hydrogen evolved and OH⁻ generated; Na⁺ migrates in, giving NaOH solution (~10–12%).…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The cell is three products and a separation problem - each product destroys another if they meet, so the diaphragm IS the product specification.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Overall: 2NaCl + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + Cl2 + H2 (electrolysis). Anode (graphite/Ti): 2Cl- -> Cl2 + 2e-. Cathode (steel mesh): 2H2O + 2e- -> H2 + 2OH-; NaOH ~10-12% with ~1% NaCl. Diaphragm (asbestos): porous, brine percolates anode->cathode; prevents Cl2 + NaOH -> NaCl + NaClO (+NaClO3).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Chlorine often drives the cell's economics - PVC, bleach and disinfectants pay for the caustic soda.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Deep Conceptual — The Cell Is Three Products and a Separation Problem - The electrolysis of brine produces **three sellable products at three electrodes/spaces:** Cl₂ (anode space), H₂ (cathode space), NaOH (cathode solution).…  ·  ## 4. Deep Conceptual — Why the Diaphragm Must Percolate - The diaphragm is porous and brine **flows through it** from anode to cathode side: the flow's purpose is to sweep Na⁺ (and NaOH) to the cathode side while its bulk keeps the hydroxide from back-diffusing to the anode.…  ·  ## 5. Worked Example Types - **Type A — cell description:** electrodes, half-equations, diaphragm role. - **Type B — the discharge competition:** why Cl₂ at the anode, H₂ at the cathode. - **Type C — the no-diaphragm consequence:** write the parasitic reaction. - **Type D — the two-cell contrast:** aqueous diaphragm cell vs molten Downs cell.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Write the reaction that would consume the products if the diaphragm failed.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **"Sodium metal forms at the cathode":** never in aqueous solution — water discharges first; Na metal requires molten NaCl (Downs). **"The diaphragm is an insulator":** it is a *selective barrier* — ions and brine pass; the gases and products must not mix.
